etymologies.etymologyHTML: From length +‎ -y.

definitions.definition: Having length; long and overextended, especially in time rather than dimension.

quote.citation: 2011 July 19, Ella Davies, “Sticks insects survive one million years without sex”, in BBC‎[1]:
quote.text: They traced the ancient lineages of two species to reveal the insects' lengthy history of asexual reproduction.

definitions.definition: Speaking or writing at length; long-winded.

quote.citation: 1863, John Cumming, Driftwood, seaweed and fallen leaves, volume 1, page 92:
quote.text: If, in addition to being a lengthy preacher, he had also been a Rev. Mr. Mumbles or a Rev. Dr. Drone, the penance thus endured by his people would have been intolerably severe.
